title: Ectoplasmic Net Formation in Aurantiochytrium limacinum
author: Anbarasu Karthikaichamy
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bc7hizj6

steps.title: Plate cells on d‑GPY agar
steps.instruction: Prepare d‑GPY agar plates according to the supplied recipe, add appropriate antibiotics, then pipette 150 µL of a 3‑day‑old Aurantiochytrium limacinum culture grown on GPY media onto each plate and spread evenly. Incubate the plates at 25 °C overnight (≈24 h).

steps.title: Add artificial seawater and incubate
steps.instruction: After the overnight incubation, add enough artificial seawater containing appropriate antibiotics to completely cover each plate. Incubate the plates at 25 °C for exactly 3 hours (03:00:00) without disturbing them. Following incubation, withdraw a small aliquot from the seawater layer and examine it for zoospores; zoospore production begins at ~90 min and peaks around 3 h.

steps.title: Transfer zoospores to slide in A1 media
steps.instruction: In a sterile petri dish, place a sterile microscope slide (or a cover slip). Add just enough A1 media with appropriate antibiotics to immerse the slide. Aspirate 50 µL–100 µL of the zoospore suspension from the plate without disturbing the plate, and gently dispense the zoospores over the immersed slide. Cover the petri dish and incubate at 25 °C overnight.

steps.title: Observe ectoplasmic net formation
steps.instruction: The next day, examine the slide for ectoplasmic net (EN) formation; EN begins to appear after ~90 min of incubation on the slide. For time‑lapse microscopy, allow zoospores to settle on a glass‑bottom petri dish and image overnight.
